data.current_description:
Keyless evaluation path, now throttled rather than unlimited.

The per minute limit alone only stopped a fast loop; a patient one could
still mint keys forever from one address. A daily cap per address makes the
free tier cost a new IP per handful of keys. Anyone who needs more than that
legitimately makes an account, where the limits are per account instead.

No email or payment information required.

data.current_description:
A hosted MCP server over the streamable HTTP transport, speaking JSON-RPC 2.0. Add it to Claude Code with:

```
claude mcp add --transport http neurobird-search https://search.neurobird.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```

The same URL works in any MCP client that supports streamable HTTP, including Cursor, Windsurf, Zed and the Claude desktop app.

Methods: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`.
Tools: `web_search` (ranked sources with page passages already extracted) and `extract_url` (any page as clean markdown).
data.summary_suggestion: Access Neurobird search tools via Model Context Protocol
data.description_suggestion: Exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over streamable HTTP using JSON-RPC 2.0 transport. Requires authentication via Bearer token in the Authorization header. Provides two tools: `web_search` (returns ranked search results with extracted page passages) and `extract_url` (converts any webpage to clean markdown). Supports standard MCP methods: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, and `ping`. Compatible with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, and Claude desktop app. Use this endpoint to integrate Neurobird search capabilities into MCP-compatible AI development environments.

data.current_description:
Answer an unpaid GET with the same 402 challenge the POST route issues.

This route used to 405. Directory crawlers and x402 explorers probe a paid
resource with a plain GET to read its terms, and a 405 carries no price, no
network and no pay-to address, so the resource looks broken rather than
priced. The challenge is metadata about the resource, not about the search
operation, so serving it on GET is both more discoverable and more correct.
Actually running a search still requires POST with a query.

This allows agents to discover payment requirements and available payment protocols before attempting a search. Actual search execution requires POST with a query parameter.

data.current_description:
The same search, but always priced.

`/search` keeps a free demo lane, which means it answers 200 to an
unauthenticated caller and is therefore not a payment-required resource in
the protocol sense. This route always issues a challenge, so agents and the
MPP and x402 registries have an endpoint whose terms are unambiguous.

Both protocols are offered on the same 402: an MPP challenge in
`WWW-Authenticate: Payment` and an x402 challenge in `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`.
data.summary_suggestion: Search the web with guaranteed payment

Accepts the same SearchRequest parameters as the standard search endpoint. Returns a 402 response with payment terms in WWW-Authenticate (MPP) and PAYMENT-REQUIRED (x402) headers when payment is required.

data.current_description:
Keyless evaluation path, now throttled rather than unlimited.

The per minute limit alone only stopped a fast loop; a patient one could
still mint keys forever from one address. A daily cap per address makes the
free tier cost a new IP per handful of keys. Anyone who needs more than that
legitimately makes an account, where the limits are per account instead.
data.description_suggestion: Creates a free API key without requiring signup or authentication. The key includes 1,000 free credits per month. Rate limits apply: per-minute throttling and a daily cap per IP address to prevent abuse. Returns the new API key and credit balance. Use this key in the Authorization header as 'Bearer nbs-...' or in the x-api-key header for subsequent API calls.
